# aeneid-071 (IX.717–818) — drafter's notes

51 units; `make_units.py` runs clean (no LINE COUNT / TOO LONG / NEWLINE / ENDING / NOTE LENGTH warnings). `t` comes only
from `A.cut`; no `sc`. Every note is under 140 words (longest 121: the 801–805 unit; then 118, 727–730). Two units are
five lines (722–726, 792b–796 the lion simile, 801–805); 771b–773 ends at a comma (no stronger stop in 771b–776, six lines).
Paragraphs: 717, 778 (both `p: true`; each note opens "A new paragraph in Greenough."). 818 is the last line of Book IX.

Title `Turnus intra muros`; part "Turnus Inside the Walls (IX.717–818)".

## Speech marks

- Pandarus: “ 737 (`“Non haec`) … ” 739 (`potestas.”`), units 737b–738 and 739.
- Turnus: “ 741 (`“Incipe`) … ” 742 (`Achillem.”`), units 741 and 742.
- Turnus: “ 747 (`“At non`) … ” 748 (`auctor.”`), units 747–748a and 748b (no verb of speaking before it; `Sic ait` 749).
- Mnestheus: “ 781 … ” 781 (misprinted, see below), one unit; then “ 782 (`“Quos alios`) … ” 787 (`pudetque?”`).
5 “ / 5 ” in each of t, l, i. The misplaced mark at 781 stays inside the same unit as `inquit`, so no mark moves between units.

## Misprint calls (rule 5b; t as printed, l/i corrected, note opens "The print has X, a misprint for Y, corrected here.")

1. **9.781 `tenditis? ”inquit.`** for `tenditis?” inquit.` — closing mark joined to the next word, as 9.377, 9.392, 9.423
   (aeneid-067). Unit 781. No other misprints found: punctuation and capitals after stops all regular.

## Latin Library variants

None changes the sense, so none is noted in `n`:
- 724 `vi magna` / `multa`; 764 `tergum` / `tergus` (same word, other declension); 770 `desectum` ("cut off") / `deiectum`
  ("struck off") — the same picture; 782 `quae iam ultra` / `quaeve ultra`; 765 `Halym` / `Halyn`; 741 `siqua` / `si qua`
  (the note on 741 explains Greenough's one-word form); orthography (`viresque`, `volnus`, `inpubesque`, `inpune`, `ungere`,
  `aëriam`) ignored, Greenough's forms explained where they occur.

## Other things for the reviewer

- **Half-lines** 721 and 761: noted as unfinished (scanner flags 721 COSTLY and 761 UNRESOLVED for that reason; they
  need half-line scan-fixes entries as earlier parts).
- **777 bracketed spurious**, kept in [ ] inside the 774–777 unit; noted. I did not check whether the Latin Library has
  the line (no variant is listed for it).
- **746 `veniens`** taken as neuter accusative with `volnus` understood ("turned it aside as it came"), Juno as the
  alternative given.
- **800 `confusa fuga`**: the metre (third foot `gā pēr`) makes `fugā` ablative, so `confusa` goes with `agmina`. Please
  confirm the scansion: bīs cōn | fū-să fŭ | gā pēr | mū-rōs | āg-mĭ-nă | vēr-tit.
- **748 `neque enim is`**: two elisions, `nequ(e) enim`, `en(im) is` (15 syllables, 6 feet).
- **752 `concussa est`**: prodelision named in the note.
- **767**: Alcandrumqu(e) Haliumque elision; fifth foot `quē Prŭ-tă` with `-que` lengthened before `Pr`. Worth a hand scan.
- **811** (flagged COSTLY): I make it īc-tĭ-bŭs | īn-gĕ-mĭ | nānt hās | tīs ēt | Trō-ĕs ĕt | īp-se, which looks like what
  the scanner gives; `Troes` two syllables (also 756).
- Greek eu: `Teucri` 719, 779, 791; `Mnestheus` 779, 781, 812; `Lyncea` (768) is Lyn-ce-a, not eu. Ae-: `Aeneadae` 735,
  `Aeneae` 787, `Aeoliden` 774. Consonantal i after prefix: 807 `iniectis`. Also 787 `magn(i) Aeneae`, 782 `i(am) ultra`.
- 810–811 `umbo / ictibus`: no elision across the line end (not listed).
- Interpretations hedged in notes: 730 `non` taken with `viderit`; 770 `dexter` adverbial "on the right"; 773 the list's
  verb understood; 805 `ni Turnus cedat` as the reported threat.

## Advisory: none

Pandarus's head split in two (750–755) is battle killing in Homer's manner; 067 (beheading, spear through temples), 068
(heads on spears) and 070 (arrow through the head) took none, and only 063 (Sabine women, Mettus) has one. QUESTIONS item
61 (a ruling on battle violence in IX–XII) is still open. A ready lede if wanted: "Turnus kills Pandarus with a sword-blow
that splits his head in two, the halves hanging over either shoulder (750–755)."
